title: Trace Patchwork Standup - week of 2026-06-14
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a compact standup-ish notebook for the "trace patchwork" mini-sprint focused on three things: tighten dashboard signal (reduce noise), validate sampling knobs against cost targets, and patch a handful of high-cardinality spans that are blowing our storage costs. Use this as the canonical week-of notes and lightweight decision record.

Quick TL;DR (top-line):
- Sampling playtest reduced ingested span volume by ~38% in the experimental pool (see metrics below) with negligible change in SLO alert noise.
- Two problematic span types identified (http:upstream-proxy and transformer:kv-lookup) — added temporary aggregation and tag-pruning in the agent.
- Dashboard "top offenders" view updated; UX feedback from Infra shows it surfaces cost drivers more clearly but needs clearer time-range defaults.

Standup snippets (daily capture):
Mon 2026-06-14:
- Maya: landed initial sampling config patch (sample_rate=0.6 for user-facing routes) in trace-agent branch. Running small canary.
- Ethan: built dashboard tile (Top span types by token-count) and added cost-per-span annotation. Draft at GH PR 472.
- Sofia: ran quick query to map span cardinality -> daily cost; identified ~6k unique keys for transformer:kv-lookup.
- Action: Priya to prototype tag-drop rule for non-essential headers.

Tue 2026-06-15:
- Canary results: 36% reduction in spans for canary app with no increase in 4xx/5xx alerts. CPU on agent unchanged.
- Found bad client behavior: an internal library emitting redundant context spans on retry path; flagged to platform eng (OBS-921).
- Decided to add an agent-side dedup window of 200ms for identical span fingerprints.
- Action: Liam to implement fingerprint dedupe, ETA Thu 6/17.

Wed 2026-06-16 (sync with Infra):
- UX notes: "Top offenders" tile useful but confusing when time-range = "auto" (defaults to 6h). Infra wants 24h default for cost investigations.
- Decided: dashboards default time-range -> 24h for cost view; keep 6h for latency view. Ethan to update dashboard JSON.

Thu 2026-06-17:
- Priya validated tag-drop rule: dropping header.x-trace-debug reduced cardinality in transformer:kv-lookup by ~22%. Good stop-gap.
- Dedupe window implemented in branch; initial unit tests pass. Integration test on canary tomorrow.
- Cost estimate: if rules are applied cluster-wide, projected monthly trace storage saving ~12-15% (~$9k/month). Conservative estimate pending final rollout.

Friday retro notes (quick):
- What went well: fast iteration cycle (canary -> metrics -> dashboard) and tight cross-team handoffs.
- What didn't: sparse test coverage around span fingerprint collisions; need a harness to simulate high-cardinality churn.
- Follow-ups: build synthetic span churn harness (owner: Sofia, due 2026-06-28).

Instrumentation & queries (snippets + rationale):
- Query used to map cardinality -> cost (pseudo-QL):
  SELECT span.type, count(DISTINCT span.key) as unique_keys, sum(storage_bytes) as bytes
  FROM traces
  WHERE timestamp >= now() - 7d
  GROUP BY span.type
  ORDER BY bytes DESC
- Rationale: we care less about total span count and more about unique key churn because storage cost scales with cardinality.

Open decisions and notes:
- Sampling policy: keep canary config (0.6) and expand to non-critical internal routes next week if canary stable for 72h. Owner: Maya.
- Dedupe window: 200ms is conservative. If we see reduced duplication, consider lowering to 100ms to avoid masking true bursts. Owner: Liam.
- Dashboard defaults: update saved views and add a short help text explaining time-range choices. Owner: Ethan.

Action items (explicit list):
- Maya: widen sampling canary to 5 services by 2026-06-18 and report span delta. (in_progress)
- Liam: merge dedupe-window change after canary integration test; add metrics for false-positive suppression. (blocking: test infra)
- Priya: harden tag-drop rules and add unit tests for tag-parsing edge cases by 2026-06-21. (todo)
- Sofia: build synthetic churn harness and wire it to CI (2026-06-28). (todo)
- Ethan: push dashboard time-range default change + help blurb (2026-06-19). (todo)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: over-aggressive sampling may hide low-frequency bugs. Mitigation: keep a held-out reservoir (2% deterministic capture) of traces for debugging.
- Risk: dedupe window could collapse legitimate concurrent spans. Mitigation: metrics for dedupe suppression rate + manual sampling retention.

Notes-to-self / unanswered questions:
- Could we integrate a light-weight bloom filter on the agent to reduce cardinality before sending? Prototype idea but CPU tradeoffs unknown. (R&D ticket?)
- Do we want a costs-by-team breakdown in the cost view, or keep it per-service only? Requesting product input.

Attachments / links referenced:
- GH PR (dashboard): github.com/redwood-inference/infra-observability/pull/472
- Trace agent branch (sampling + dedupe): github.com/redwood-inference/trace-agent/compare/patch/sampling-dedupe
- JIRA ticket for client library emitting retries: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OBS-921

Final quick log:
- Week outcome: shipped conservative config changes that materially reduce trace ingest and gave a clear path for additional ~10% savings next quarter if applied with tag-pruning and dedupe.
- Next checkpoint: 2026-06-21 sync — bring canary delta graphs, dedupe integration result, and dashboard PR ready for staging review.

-- end of notes (informal; may be expanded into formal runbook if changes are approved)
